records.title: 1420 · Tábor founded in Bohemia
records.note: Radical Hussites established Tábor and named the settlement after biblical Mount Tabor. The official city account records its Hussite origin and later church dedicated to the Transfiguration.

records.title: Scripture, worship and community
records.note: Sources describe radical Hussite reforms, a strong scriptural basis, changes to worship and an early communal experiment. Track individual articles and factions before generalizing the reforms to every resident or to the full history of Tábor.

records.title: 1434 · Battle of Lipany
records.note: A coalition including Catholic and moderate Utraquist forces defeated the radical forces. Treat Lipany as a dated military and political event within a longer institutional history.

records.title: 1452 · George of Poděbrady takes Tábor
records.note: Tábor remained a center after Lipany. George of Poděbrady took the town in 1452. The military defeat and later loss of autonomy belong on separate timeline entries.

records.title: Tábor ⇄ family descent or the Order of Twelve
records.note: Documented biblical naming gives a real textual link. A claim that the town's movement passed into Nathan Tabor’s family or Moses Dickson’s order requires dated ties from both ends of the proposed chain.
